survey: An orange wall clock, seen almost straight on against a flat green striped wall. Its thick, rounded orange rim sits flat against the wall and drops a soft shadow down and to the right, which fits a light from the upper left and a wall directly behind the clock. The white dial is set slightly into the rim. The rim and the dial are both near-circular ellipses with the same slight squash, so they agree on one nearly frontal viewpoint. The 12 hour ticks and the ring of minute dots point straight out from the center and are evenly spaced around the dial. Each one shows the same small extruded side and drop shadow, so they all match the dial's angle. The hour, minute and red second hands share one pivot cap at the dial's center, which is also the rim's center. They lie flat in a plane just above the dial, and their shadows fall the same way as the ticks' shadows. The background stripes are vertical and parallel, which fits a flat wall seen straight on.
